basis: 24 of 25 tracked indices rose in their latest session.
VIX closed at 17.49 (-10.12% on the day).
Rule: Risk-on = 65%+ of indices up and VIX not rising; Risk-off = 35% or fewer up, or VIX up 8%+; otherwise Mixed.

headline.technical: WSJ reported a $2.5 trillion AI-led rout in US tech; the S&P 500 recovered only 0.31% on the day and is down 2.68% over five days, with the VIX at 25.64 and rate-hike expectations firming after the jobs report.
headline.layman: Tech and AI stocks had a historic sell-off this week and the rebound was weak. Fear in markets is elevated, and investors now expect the US central bank may raise rates.

global.title: AI sell-off dominates; rebound is tepid

status.technical: WSJ called it a $2.5 trillion AI reality check and FT a $3.2tn rout; FT said the rebound was feeble versus historic recoveries. S&P 500 +0.31% on the day, -2.68% over 5 days; Nasdaq +1.09%, drawdown from 52w high -10.94%; VIX 25.64, up 32.03% over 5 days.
status.layman: Stocks tied to AI fell hard earlier this week. Friday brought a small bounce, but the Nasdaq is still down about 11% from its high and the market's fear gauge is much higher than a week ago.

consequence.technical: FT said investors are no longer pricing in accelerating AI growth, and WSJ said systematic trades amplified losses. If those flows reverse or the tech slide resumes, volatility could stay elevated; if tech stabilises, the VIX could ease.
consequence.layman: If investors keep rethinking AI, wild swings could continue. If tech settles down, the fear gauge could calm.

impact.technical: Yahoo Finance noted the hit to 401(k) balances; CNBC reported ING reportedly seeking bids for about $500 million of data center loans, a sign of AI debt concern. Evidence on wider credit effects is thin.
impact.layman: Retirement savings invested in tech took a hit, and a bank is reportedly trying to sell some data center loans. The notes do not show broader damage yet.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the S&P 500 rose the next day 54% of 846 times and over the next 5 days 59% of 844 times (10th-90th pct -2.3% to 2.68%). After VIX look-alike days it fell over the next 5 days in 5 of 5 cases (median -21.52%).
outlook.layman: Not a forecast. In past days like this, the S&P 500 rose over the next week 59% of the time (844 cases), though results varied widely.

regions.title: Americas: Nasdaq in correction, small bounce

status.technical: Closes: S&P 500 +0.31%, Nasdaq +1.09%, Dow -0.46%. Straits Times said the Nasdaq posted a fourth straight weekly decline; CNBC said it slid into correction territory. Reuters said TSX futures slipped on tech jitters ahead of employment data.
status.layman: US stocks bounced a little on Friday, but the Nasdaq has now fallen four weeks in a row and is in what is called a correction (a drop of roughly a tenth from its peak).

consequence.technical: If the Fed hike expectations FT and CNBC describe grow, pressure on tech could persist; Reuters flagged US inflation data in the week ahead as the next test. If inflation surprises lower, that pressure could ease.
consequence.layman: If investors expect higher interest rates, tech could stay under pressure. Next week's inflation report is the next test.

impact.technical: Tech-heavy portfolios and retirement-account holders took the hit; the Dow fell 0.46% on the day. Notes give no sector-level contribution breakdown.
impact.layman: People with lots of tech stock were hurt most. The notes do not say how much each company mattered.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary days the Nasdaq rose the next 5 days 59% of 824 times (median 0.61%); look-alike days rose 4 of 5 times over the next 21 days (median 4.65%).
outlook.layman: Not a forecast. After typical days the Nasdaq rose over the next week 59% of the time (824 cases).

regions.title: Europe: weekly loss as AI rout spreads

status.technical: Reuters said the FTSE 100 posted a weekly loss as AI jitters sparked a risk-off move; the index closed down 1.01% on the day. Reuters also said European shares fell as the AI rout gathered pace, and WSJ said eurozone retail sales slumped as high energy prices hit confidence.
status.layman: European stocks fell as the AI sell-off spread. Britain's FTSE 100 lost ground for the week, and eurozone shoppers cut spending because of high energy costs.

consequence.technical: If energy costs stay high, as WSJ describes, consumer spending could stay weak; Yahoo Finance UK said the BoE raised interest rates, which could add to pressure on borrowers. Eurozone yields dropped per Yahoo Finance.
consequence.layman: If energy stays expensive, shoppers could keep cutting back. A Bank of England rate rise adds to pressure on borrowers.

impact.technical: Consumer-facing companies and borrowers are exposed per the notes; the notes give no specific sector breakdown for equities.
impact.layman: Shoppers and people with loans are most affected, according to the notes.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day falls above 1 standard deviation the FTSE 100 rose the next day 54% of 158 times and over the next 5 days 64% of 157 times (median 0.41%).
outlook.layman: Not a forecast. After sharp drops like this, the FTSE 100 rose over the following week 64% of the time (157 cases).

regions.title: Asia-Pacific: AI trade unwinds, authorities step in

status.technical: FT said the Nikkei 225 and Topix dropped nearly 6%, the biggest one-day fall since 'liberation day'. WSJ said Taiwan joined South Korea in market-stabilisation measures. SCMP said the CSI 300 fell 1.4 per cent and China's 10-year bond hit a record low. Business Standard said Indian indices posted their best week in 6 years.
status.layman: Japan had its worst day in a long time as investors fled AI stocks. Taiwan and South Korea stepped in to calm their markets. India was the exception, with its best week in about six years.

consequence.technical: If the global AI selloff resumes, chip-heavy markets could face renewed pressure and further intervention; WSJ linked Taiwan and Korea measures to the selloff. If Wall Street's Friday bounce holds, some pressure could ease.
consequence.layman: If the AI sell-off returns, markets with many chip companies could be hit again. If Wall Street steadies, Asia could calm too.

impact.technical: Bloomberg said Taiwan's currency weakened past 33 per US dollar on AI jitters; chip-exposed indices are most affected per Mint. Indian equities moved against the trend in the notes.
impact.layman: Taiwan's currency weakened, and countries with big chip industries felt it most. India moved the other way.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day falls above 1 standard deviation the Nikkei rose the next day 55% of 162 times and over the next 5 days 58% of 161 times; KOSPI rose the next day 55% of 152 times.
outlook.layman: Not a forecast. After big drops like this, Japan's market rose the next day 55% of the time (162 cases).

drivers.title: AI valuation reset after the US midterms

status.technical: WSJ said Democrats' victories supercharged anxieties building for weeks, with systematic trades amplifying losses. Mint said the sweep triggered a massive sell-off in AI and semiconductor stocks. FT said investors no longer price in accelerating AI growth. Nasdaq drawdown from 52w high is -10.94%.
status.layman: After the election, investors worried that new rules could slow AI spending. They sold AI and chip stocks hard, and automated trading made it worse.

consequence.technical: If investors keep reassessing AI growth, per FT, tech could remain volatile; OpenAI's CFO told CNBC it will keep investing in data centers despite the election results, which would be a counterweight if others follow.
consequence.layman: If doubts about AI spending persist, tech could stay shaky. OpenAI says it is still investing, which could help steady things.

impact.technical: Chipmakers, AI infrastructure and data-center lenders are exposed; ING is reportedly selling about $500 million of data center loans, per CNBC. Evidence on other sectors is thin.
impact.layman: Chip firms, AI builders and their lenders are most exposed. The notes say little about other industries.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: Nasdaq rose the next 5 days 59% of 824 times after ordinary days; VIX look-alike days fell over the next 21 days in 5 of 5 cases (median -17.20%).
outlook.layman: Not a forecast. In similar past periods the Nasdaq rose over the next week 59% of the time (824 cases).

drivers.title: Fed rate-hike expectations after the jobs report

status.technical: FT said the US added 165,000 jobs in October, reinforcing expectations the Fed will raise rates; CNBC quoted San Francisco Fed's Daly saying more rate hikes are likely. Morningstar separately headlined a third straight monthly jobs decline and rising unemployment. US 10-year yield closed at 4.86; dollar index +0.72%.
status.layman: A strong jobs report made investors expect the US central bank may raise interest rates again. Reports differ on jobs, so the picture is mixed.

consequence.technical: If next week's inflation data, flagged by Morningstar, runs hot, rate-hike bets could grow; Dow daily moves have correlated -0.37 with the 10-year yield over the past year.
consequence.layman: If next week's inflation report is high, more rate hikes could be expected. That tends to weigh on stocks.

impact.technical: Reuters said the Canadian dollar hit a nearly three-week low on a surprise jobs loss; gold fell on the strong US jobs data per the notes. Households face the inflation pressure Daly described.
impact.layman: Households feel higher prices, and gold fell on the jobs news. Canada's currency weakened after a surprise drop in jobs there.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day dollar index rises above 1 standard deviation it rose the next day 51% of 187 times and over the next 5 days 52% of 187 times.
outlook.layman: Not a forecast. After big dollar jumps, the next week was close to a coin flip (52% up, 187 cases).

drivers.title: Oil: weekly drop but still high

status.technical: Business Standard said Brent sank the most in a week since Covid; Brent closed at 97.76, down 16.90% over 5 days but up 60.66% year to date. Business Standard also said Brent rose 60.4% in Samvat 2082 amid the US-Iran conflict.
status.layman: Oil had its biggest weekly drop since the pandemic, but is still far more expensive than at the start of the year.

consequence.technical: WSJ said high energy prices continue to weigh on eurozone consumers. If oil falls further, that pressure could ease; if it rebounds, the pressure would remain.
consequence.layman: If oil keeps falling, European shoppers could get relief. If it climbs again, they will not.

impact.technical: Oil importers such as India benefit from lower prices: Business Standard said the rupee shone across Asia. Eurozone retail sales slumped per WSJ.
impact.layman: Countries that import oil, like India, gain when oil falls. Europe's shoppers are still feeling the high prices.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: Brent look-alike days rose over the next 5 days 4 of 5 times (median 3.37%); after ordinary days it rose 51% of 846 times over 5 days, with a 10th-90th pct range of -5.77% to 6.24%.
outlook.layman: Not a forecast. Oil is hard to call: after typical days it rose over the next week 51% of the time (846 cases).

drivers.title: Central banks: BoE hikes, RBA and BoJ in focus

status.technical: Yahoo Finance UK reported the Bank of England raised interest rates. WSJ said the RBA is preparing another rate rise. Bloomberg said BoJ Governor Ueda called it unclear how long 2% inflation will last. WSJ said Bank of Mexico cut its benchmark rate in a split decision. ECB deposit rate: 2.5 %.
status.layman: Central banks are going different ways: Britain raised rates, Australia may raise again, and Mexico cut rates in a split vote.

consequence.technical: If more central banks tighten, as the BoE and a prospective RBA move suggest, financial conditions could tighten for borrowers; if inflation proves transient, as Ueda's comment leaves open, tightening could pause.
consequence.layman: If more central banks raise rates, borrowing gets costlier. If inflation fades, they could pause.

impact.technical: WSJ said Australia's housing slump is deepening ahead of the RBA move. Borrowers are most exposed. Evidence on bank earnings is thin.
impact.layman: People with mortgages are most exposed. Australia's housing market is already weakening.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: the S&P/ASX 200 rose the next 5 days 55% of 858 times after ordinary days (10th-90th pct -2% to 2.09%).
outlook.layman: Not a forecast. After typical days, Australia's market rose over the next week 55% of the time (858 cases).

events.title: US inflation data
events.technical: Reuters and Morningstar said US inflation data in the coming week could give clues on rate-hike prospects.
events.layman: A US inflation report next week could shape expectations for interest rates.

events.title: RBI 4-day Variable Rate Repo auction
events.technical: The RBI said it will conduct a 4-day VRR auction under LAF on Monday, November 09, 2026, with a notified amount of ₹50,000 crore, citing liquidity conditions.
events.layman: India's central bank will lend ₹50,000 crore for four days on Monday to manage cash in the banking system.
